sections.html:
Parkersburg is the Wood County seat, where the Little Kanawha River meets the Ohio. The 2020 census counted 29,738 residents, fourth in the state, and the Parkersburg and Vienna metro area holds 89,490. Numbers have fallen in every census since 1960, when the city had 44,797. The city covers about 12.35 square miles.

The Little Kanawha splits the city into a north side and a south side. South Parkersburg was its own city until it joined in 1950. Most named neighborhoods are on the north side, and each has its own housing style:

  • Downtown, Julia-Ann Square and Quincy Hill
  • Beechwood, Fairview Heights and Granada Hills
  • Meadowcrest, Oakwood Estates and Woodland Park
  • Riverside, Worthington and the East End

South of the river, the former city of South Parkersburg runs into suburban southern Wood County: Blennerhassett, Lubeck and Washington to the southwest and Mineral Wells to the southeast. Some of those sit outside the city, so tax and code rules differ by address.

Chemicals, finance and federal work drive local jobs. DuPont, Highmark, United Bank and Woodcraft are known employers, and the U.S. Treasury's Bureau of the Fiscal Service employs more than 2,000 people here. Jobs like these bring people in and out of the area, which is part of why homes change hands. West Virginia University at Parkersburg adds some rental demand.

The Parkersburg Floodwall shields low parts of the city along the Ohio and Little Kanawha rivers, and owners inside the protected zone pay a maintenance fee. Article 783 of the city code treats those owners as the users and beneficiaries of the wall, who bear the cost of its continuance, maintenance and improvement. It also sets a payment schedule and penalties, and the Director of Finance administers it. The city's codified ordinances carry the full text.

Floodwall ruleWhat the city code provides
Protected flood zoneProperties at or below about 624 feet above sea level, protected by the floodwall
Boundary set byThe City Engineer
Fees paid byOwners of property in the zone
Administered byDirector of Finance
Residential buildingExcludes rentals of four or more units on one tract

If you are selling inside the zone, ask whether any floodwall fees are unpaid, since the code carries penalties, and have the title company check whether a balance affects the closing. Any address can be checked on the state's flood map tool.

The city's Code Enforcement Division enforces building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Its aim is voluntary compliance from owners, with further steps when that fails. See the division's page.

A separate Building Enforcement Agency meets on the first Monday of each month at 9:00 a.m. The Mayor, the City Engineer and the Code Enforcement Director sit on it, and it works on neglected, vacant and abandoned properties. State law backs this up: West Virginia Code section 8-12-16c lets a municipality set up a vacant building registration and maintenance program by ordinance.

  • Keep grass and exterior debris under control while a house sits empty.
  • Answer any notice from the division in writing and keep a copy.
  • Ask the division about open complaints before you sign a sale contract.

An heir who inherits a neglected house and cannot pay for repairs may find a direct sale simpler than a repair schedule. Cash Home Buyers looks at each Parkersburg property as is, with no obligation if you decline an offer.

sections.h2: Why is my house taxed as non-residential?
sections.html:
Wood County assesses and taxes Parkersburg property, and you pay real estate tax at the Wood County Sheriff's office, not the Assessor. The Assessor values property as of July 1. Your bill is a levy rate times your assessed value, which is 60 percent of market value. The legislature sets levy rates for the Board of Education, the county commission and the municipalities.

Two rules catch owners off guard:

  • A home deeded to an LLC cannot be taxed as Class 2 residential, so all LLC-owned property is Class 3 or 4.
  • Class 2 requires an owner-occupied home with the owner's name on the deed, so a relative living in another home you own does not qualify.

Either one can change the bill a buyer expects, so ask the assessor how your house is classed before you list.

For an inherited house, the original owner's classification may no longer apply once the home is empty or rented. Call the Assessor's office, give the parcel details and ask what class applies today, then pass that answer to anyone who makes an offer.

sections.h2: Due dates and the transfer tax
sections.html:
State dates apply. Bills issue on or after July 15, the first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1. Pay early for a 2.5 percent discount, and late amounts carry 9 percent annual interest. The Tax Division page has the schedule.

At sale, the transfer excise tax under section 11-22-2 is $1.10 per $500 of value. A county excise tax of 55 cents per $500 is added, and counties can raise it. The seller normally pays, and a $20 fee goes to the state Affordable Housing Fund.

Many sales here involve an heir who lives elsewhere. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary, so you rarely need to travel. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded, and keep a short list of what you need from the county before you start.

  • the latest tax statement and the sheriff's balance
  • any open notices from Code Enforcement
  • floodwall fee status, if the house is inside the zone
  • the deed or probate papers

On closing day the title company pays off any mortgage, floodwall balance and tax owed from your proceeds, the deed is recorded with the county, and the remainder is sent to you. If you cannot attend, ask that the documents be mailed to you or signed before a remote notary in advance, and get the payoff figures in writing a few days ahead so nothing surprises you at the end.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so you skip arranging repairs, showings and a lender's timeline from a distance. Compare what a sale leaves after taxes, liens and transfer costs, and decline any offer that does not work for you.

Interstate 77 and US 50 are the main highways, and WV routes 2, 14, 47, 68, 95 and 618 also pass through the city. The Mid-Ohio Valley Regional Airport has three flights a day on weekdays from Charlotte. Passenger trains stopped in the 1960s, with Amtrak's Shenandoah running from 1976 to 1981, and CSX still provides freight service.

faqs.q: Does the Parkersburg floodwall fee affect my sale?
faqs.a: It can if your property is inside the protected flood zone. Article 783 of the city code puts the maintenance cost on those owners and sets penalties, so ask the city's finance office whether anything is unpaid before closing.

faqs.q: Who do I call about code problems on a vacant Parkersburg house?
faqs.a: The city's Building and Code Enforcement department handles building, health and safety, zoning and nuisance codes. Contact it before you sell so any open notice is known.

faqs.q: Why is my Parkersburg house taxed as non-residential?
faqs.a: West Virginia allows Class 2 residential status only for an owner-occupied home with the owner's name on the deed. A house deeded to an LLC is taxed as Class 3 or 4.

faqs.q: When are Wood County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, with delinquency starting October 1 and April 1. Pay the Wood County Sheriff, not the Assessor.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Parkersburg house if I live out of state?
faqs.a: Yes. Title companies can handle signing by mail or remote notary. Confirm who is arranging the closing and how the deed will be recorded.
